title: Fusion balance-of-plant heat conversion
bottleneck: Fusion blankets deliver heat at 300 to 700 degrees Celsius depending on coolant choice, and converting that heat to electricity efficiently requires power cycles matched to fusion's unique constraints: tritium-contaminated coolants, pulsed operation, and massive thermal inertia. Supercritical CO2 and advanced Rankine cycles promise higher efficiency but are unproven at fusion-relevant scale and temperatures. Every point of conversion efficiency lost multiplies the required fusion power.
why_it_blocks: Fusion's economics are hostage to thermal efficiency. At 30 percent conversion a plant must produce far more fusion power, and survive far more neutron damage, than at 45 percent.
current_state: Supercritical CO2 pilot plants are advancing for other applications. No fusion-specific power conversion system has been built or tested with tritium-bearing coolants.

sources.title: Reliable Nuclear Fusion Will Require New Heat- and Radiation-Resilient Materials
